guide.headline: Chiefs run defense and Raiders third downs decide this one
guide.hook: The Chiefs defense erases the run and strangles passing downs, so watch whether the Raiders can survive long enough to let their rookie corner and his three interceptions matter.

items.title: Chiefs run D versus Raiders run game
items.what: The Chiefs rank No. 5 of 32 against the run at a 33% success rate, while the Raiders rank No. 29 in rush success at 32%. That is a 77 percentile point gap, not a lean. If the Raiders can't get push on the ground, they get shoved into obvious passing downs where this defense feasts.
items.when: First quarter, watch Raiders yards per carry; under 3 and the game plan changes
items.who: Raiders run game vs Chiefs run defense

items.title: Raiders on long passing downs
items.what: The Raiders rank No. 26 of 32 on passing downs at 30% success, and the Chiefs defense ranks No. 13 at 35%. That is a 42 percentile point edge for Kansas City, and it compounds the run game problem by pushing Las Vegas into exactly the situations they are worst at.
items.when: Third-and-7 or longer for the Raiders
items.who: Raiders on passing downs vs Chiefs pressure

items.title: Hezekiah Masses hunting the ball
items.what: Masses is a rookie fifth round pick, No. 175 overall, playing like a top pick with 3 interceptions, 4 pass deflections and 8 tackles, top 1 percent production for an NFL cornerback. He is the No. 1 right cornerback on the depth chart at 64% of defensive snaps, so if the Chiefs are forced into obvious passing downs by their own run struggles, he is the man on the island who could turn a stalled Chiefs drive into a turnover.
items.when: Any third-and-long throw into his side of the field

guide.cardLine: The Chiefs erase the run and own passing downs, setting up rookie ball hawk Hezekiah Masses and his three interceptions to steal the headline.
